patches.now: apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends postgresql postgresql-client && sed -i -E 's/(scram-sha-256|md5|peer)$/trust/' /etc/postgresql/*/main/pg_hba.conf && service postgresql start && until pg_isready -h localhost; do sleep 1; done && psql -h localhost -U postgres -c "CREATE DATABASE job_scheduler;"
patches.reason: The psql client installed fine, but the container has no PostgreSQL server listening on localhost:5432, hence 'Connection refused'. The fix installs the server, sets local auth to trust because the postgres user has no password, starts the service, waits until it is ready, then runs the original psql command unchanged.

The traceback shows SQLAlchemy using its psycopg (v3) dialect, which does `import psycopg`. That package isn't installed in the venv, so the install is a missing prerequisite. `psycopg[binary]` ships a prebuilt libpq, so it needs no system libraries on python:3.11-slim. The worker command and its arguments are unchanged.
